# Text-to-(Single-or-Multi)-SQL: Bridging Real-World Needs with Spider𝕊

**Reading coverage:** All 30 pages: Sections 1–8, limitations, ethics, references and Appendices A–L, including complete theoretical assumptions, construction patterns, quality audits, efficiency/router/overlap diagnostics and image-only experiment prompts on page 30. ## Research question

Rigid single-result evaluation can reject an answer that supplies the requested information through a different query layout or several queries.

## Method

Spider𝕊 constructs clear composite requests from Spider using 14 patterns. Its evaluator projects predictions onto required columns, permits extra columns but rejects extra rows or wrong order, and maximizes one-to-one matching across predicted/gold query sets. Execution Score normalizes matched queries by the larger set size; full accuracy requires score one.

## Evaluation

The paper reports 11,746 examples, including 890 manual seeds, with GPT-4o generation and validation plus human review. Models are evaluated on full 2,147-example tests where feasible and independently sampled 1,000-example Spider and Spider𝕊 subsets. Separate experiments examine fine-tuning, a single/multi-output router, synthetic BIRD transfer, prompt sensitivity and execution costs.

## What the results support

Allowing multi-query output improves reported composite-task scores, while unnecessary extra queries lower full accuracy on ordinary Spider. Router-guided prompts mitigate this effect. Single statements have lower median latency and are faster in most measured cases, although a few large outputs make multi-query execution faster in total.

## Limits and qualifications

The task excludes ambiguous interpretations and is not an answerability test. Matching executions on one database does not prove semantic equivalence or validate relationships absent from the annotated result units. Single-query impossibility claims conflict with constructed single-statement alternatives. The displayed single-query prompt also requests separate queries. Artifact access failed, preventing implementation, licensing and dataset verification.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adjacent evaluation work on reference-format tolerance and completeness of composite answers. It should be separated from multiple interpretations, interactive clarification and unsupported-request refusal.
